submission.natural_language_explanation: The pole is a retrospective letter-w detector on the token it sits on: it fires when the measured token begins with w/W — short word-initial fragments and name pieces (' Wa', ' Wil', ' Wal', ' W', 'WH', 'wh', 'wi', the strongest of all), the written w of ordinary words ('whole', 'wolf', 'wing'; weaker but usually over the active line), and the w-letter of other scripts (kana 'ワーク'/'ワ'/'ヲ', which fires as strongly) — and the same response lands on the next token when a w ends a preceding word fragment ('ew'->'a' in Swahili, '-w'->'he' in 'two-wheeled'). It falls to the noise floor when the same slot carries the same word under any other initial letter ('Val' for 'Wal', 'golf' for 'wolf', 'short' for 'whole', 'groei' for 'werking' in Dutch), when the w sits inside the token ('answer', 'swim', 'between'), and it is weakest on the highest-frequency w-function words of running English ('was', 'with', 'will').

rival_explanations: The pole detects any word-initial fragment token (a word-opening piece that must be continued) rather than the letter w specifically: it should fire nearly as strongly on non-w fragments in the same slot such as ' Val', ' Bal' or ' Zl' as on ' Wal' or ' Wil'.

The pole is a W-initial proper-name and acronym detector (Waugh, Walz, Wilborn, Wilhelmine, Wilken, the initial ' W.', FWHM, mathcal{W}), and the lowercase prose firings on ' whole' and ' whirled' are an unrelated offshoot: w-nouns in ordinary prose should stay below the active line.

top_examples.text:
Orphanotrophos

Orphanotrophos (Greek: ὀρφανοτρόφος) was a Byzantine title for the curator of an orphanage (ὀρφανοτροφεῖον, orphanotropheion). The director of the most important orphanage, the imperial orphanage in Constantinople, established in the 4th century and lasting until the 13th century, eventually rose to become an office of particular significance and ranked among the senior ministers of the Byzantine state.

History

In the spirit of Christian philanthropy, the Byzantine world showed particular care towards the weaker members of society, including widows, orphans, the sick or the elderly. Orphans were either adopted by foster parents, or sheltered in monasteries or in orphanages, the latter often run by monasteries.

In Constantinople, the Byzantine capital, there was a particularly large orphanage in the northeastern corner of the city, at the site of the ancient acropolis of Byzantium, which eventually came under imperial patronage. According to the Patria of Constantinople, it traced its antecedents to a series of charitable establishments founded in the reign of Constans II (ruled 337 – 361) by the patrikios and protovestiarios Zotikos, for which the latter was canonized by the Church. According to a novel by Emperor Leo I the Thracian in 469, Zotikos was the first to bear the title of orphanotrophos. In the 5th century, the priest Nikon and Acacius, later Patriarch of Constantinople (472 – 488), are known to have been successively orphanotrophoi in the capital, while another future patriarch, Euphemius (489 – 495) held the post in the provincial town of Neapolis.

The legislation of Justinian I (r. 527 – 565) often mentions the orphanages and the office of orphanotrophos, but it was not until the reign of his successor Justin II (r. 565 – 578) that the institution in the capital acquired its definite characteristics: Justin and his wife Sophia, with the aid of a protovestiarios also named Zotikos, built an orphanage near the Church of St. Paul (or SS. Peter and Paul according to Theophanes the Confessor) — probably the church of the same name near the Gate of Eugenios on the sea-wall of the Golden Horn mentioned by Nikephoros Gregoras — and restored the foundation of the first Zotikos, which was possibly converted into a leprosarium. Justin bequeathed an annual stipend of 443 nomismata to the orphanage and made its possessions inalienable. It was probably then that the capital's orphanotrophos began to be appointed by the emperors. As a result, while in the provinces, the post of orphanotrophos continued to be occupied by clergymen, in the capital, it soon became a formal office and was held by members of the secular administrative hierarchy.

In the 9th – 11th centuries, the orphanotrophos' role seems to have been limited to the imperial orphanage in the capital, while the provincial charitable foundations were under the supervision of two other officials, the chartoularios tou sakelliou and the megas kourator. The orphanotropho

)

func main() {

	f, err := os.Create("/tmp/cpuprof")
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
	pprof.StartCPUProfile(f)
	defer pprof.StopCPUProfile()

	index, err := api.NewGitContentAPI()
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}

	ah := apiHandlers{index}

	m := mux.NewRouter()

	logEndpointsAndRegisterHandlers(m, "/content/recent", ah.recentHandler, "GET")
	logEndpointsAndRegisterHandlers(m, "/content/count", ah.countHandler, "GET")
	logEndpointsAndRegisterHandlers(m, "/content/{uuid}/versions/", ah.versionsHandler, "GET")
	logEndpointsAndRegisterHandlers(m, "/content/{uuid}/versions/{ver}", ah.versionHandler, "GET")
	logEndpointsAndRegisterHandlers(m, "/content/{uuid}", ah.uuidReadHandler, "GET")
	logEndpointsAndRegisterHandlers(m, "/content/{uuid}", ah.idWriteHandler, "PUT")
	logEndpointsAndRegisterHandlers(m, "/content/", ah.dropHandler, "DELETE")
	logEndpointsAndRegisterHandlers(m, "/content/", ah.dumpAllHandler, "GET")
	logEndpointsAndRegisterHandlers(m, "/article/{uuid}", ah.getArticlePageHandler, "GET")
	logEndpointsAndRegisterHandlers(m, "/article/{uuid}/versions/{version}", ah.getVersionedArticlePageHandler, "GET")
	logEndpointsAndRegisterHandlers(m, "/", ah.indexHandler, "GET")

	http.Handle("/", handlers.CombinedLoggingHandler(os.Stdout, m))

	go func() {
		port := "8082"
		fmt.Printf("listening on port: %s ...", port)
		err = http.ListenAndServe(":"+port, nil)
		if err != nil {
			log.Printf("web stuff failed: %v\n", err)
		}
	}()

	c := make(chan os.Signal, 1)
	signal.Notify(c, os.Interrupt)

	// wait for ctrl-c
	<-c
	println("exiting")
	index.Close()

	f, err = os.Create("/tmp/memprof")
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}

	pprof.WriteHeapProfile(f)
	f.Close()

	return
}

func logEndpointsAndRegisterHandlers(m *mux.Router, route string, handlerMethod func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request), httpMethod string) {
	log.Printf("Registering %[1]s %[2]s \n", httpMethod, route)
	m.HandleFunc(route, handlerMethod).Methods(httpMethod)
}

type apiHandlers struct {
	index api.ContentAPI
}

func (ah *apiHandlers) getArticlePageHandler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	vars := mux.Vars(r)
	uuid := vars["uuid"]

	found, art := ah.index.ByUUID(uuid)
	if !found {
		w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNotFound)
		w.Write([]byte(fmt.Sprintf("content with id %s was not found\n", uuid)))
		return
	}

	data := make(map[string]interface{})
	data["art"] = art
	data["versions"] = ah.index.Versions(uuid)
	renderedHTML := mustache.RenderFile("./static/article.html", data)
	io.Copy(w, strings.NewReader(renderedHTML))
}

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She ate the whole loaf on the train ride home, then complained about feeling sick for hours.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Ordinary lowercase w-initial prose word (' whole', one token) in a new narrative context: hypothesis says it usually crosses the active line, both rivals say a plain prose word should not.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The old brick wall behind the chapel was repaired last summer by a mason from the next village.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A w-noun (' wall', one token) absent from the claimed list tests whether the written w of ordinary prose words generalises beyond whole/wolf/wing.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He signed the form with a single W instead of his full first name, then slid it across the desk.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Bare capital ' W' mid-sentence as its own token, one of the claimed strongest triggers, away from any proper name.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: 来週の水曜日にワークショップ形式の会議を開きますので、資料の準備をお願いします。
adversarial_test_results.detail: Kana w-row token 'ワーク' mid-sentence in Japanese: hypothesis claims the w-letter of other scripts fires as strongly as Latin w.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Het water in de gracht steeg zo snel dat de bewoners hun boten aan de kade moesten vastmaken.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Dutch lowercase w-initial common noun, delivered as the single token ' water', tests the cross-language claim on an ordinary word rather than a name.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The crew anchored the trawler just outside the harbour and stayed aboard until the tide turned.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Retrospective carry-over on the token after a w-final fragment: ' trawler' splits as ' tr' | 'aw' | 'ler', so the token 'aw' is a word fragment ending in w and the next token 'ler' should fire, exactly the two-wheeled pattern; the word-boundary pair ' crew' | ' anchored' is a second instance of the clause.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The diaries belonged to Wilhelmine, a distant cousin, and were found in a trunk beneath the stairs.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Capitalised W name piece as its own token (' Wil' | 'hel' | 'mine'), the class rival 2 says is the real feature.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The café offered free Wi-Fi to anyone buying a pastry, which kept the students there all afternoon.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Lowercase 'wi' fragment as the strongest claimed trigger, here the token ' Wi' inside a hyphenated compound rather than a name.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The depot kept a four-wheeled cart by the loading bay and moved the crates outside at dawn.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Intra-word retrospective carry-over on the documented split: the compound gives the tokens '-w' | 'he', so the w ends a fragment and continues into the next token, and no token begins with w; the peak token ' he' is not a capitalised name piece, so rival 1's in-slot fragment rule does not fire.

Cross-genre holdout in Python: 'class' then the token ' Wave' opening the identifier 'Waveform', where hypothesis (w-initial fragment) and rival 2 (name-like) agree but the code genre is unlike the prose holdouts.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The chalet sits above the old village of Val d'Isère, and the snow there lasts until late April in most years.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same slot and same name-like fragment shape as ' Wal' but with the token ' Val': hypothesis says any other initial letter falls to the noise floor, while rival 1's in-slot fragment rule predicts a firing.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He plays golf every Sunday morning at the club near the estuary, and usually stays for lunch afterwards.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Direct swap named by the hypothesis: 'golf' as one token for 'wolf', same noun slot and topic, wrong initial letter.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: There is a short extra chapter about growing herbs on balconies, plus notes on soil, drainage and pests for beginners.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Direct swap named by the hypothesis: 'short' as one token for 'whole' in the same adjective slot, with the book-chapter topic kept.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: De groei van de economie vertraagde vorig jaar flink, en de prijzen en de lonen bleven stijgen in de grote steden.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The hypothesis's own Dutch counterfactual with 'groei' in the subject slot; the sentence contains no w character at all, so no token here begins with w whichever way it splits.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: A firm called Bal Construction bid for the contract to rebuild the eastern bridge and the two access roads.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Word-initial name fragment ' Bal' with a non-w onset, in the same slot as ' Wal': hypothesis predicts silence, rival 1 predicts a firing as strong as on ' Wal' ('won' was replaced by 'bid' because ' won' is itself a w-initial token the hypothesis would fire on).

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The striker Zlatan scored twice in the second half, and the crowd sang his name long after the final buzzer.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The rival's own example shape: a bare consonant-cluster fragment opening a proper name (' Z' | 'lat' | 'an'), but with Zl rather than W, moved mid-sentence so the fragment is a measured token rather than the probe's first token.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Nobody could answer the question about the missing ledger, so the meeting ended early.
adversarial_test_results.detail: w sits inside the single token 'answer': hypothesis says a non-initial w is at the noise floor, and no other token here begins with w.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The lane runs between two stone barns and then bends toward the river until it finally ends.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Two w-inside-the-token words ('between', 'toward') in running prose of holdout length; no token begins with w and no token ends in w either way, so the carry-over clause has nothing to fire on.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Most mornings they swim a kilometre in the cold lake before breakfast, even in October.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The token ' swim' has w in second position; tests that a word whose second letter is w does not fire like a w-initial word.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The first flower opened beside the greenhouse door, and by June the beds buzzed all day.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The single token ' flower' buries w in its final syllable: a common noun with a written w that is not word-initial, in the same garden register as the prose holdouts.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: It was a long journey, and the horses needed rest before the climb over the pass.
adversarial_test_results.detail: ' was' is named by the hypothesis as one of the weakest w-function words, so the hypothesis puts it under the active line even though it begins with w.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She travelled with her brother as far as the border, then took the night train south alone.
adversarial_test_results.detail: ' with' is named in the hypothesis's weakest w-function-word list despite the 'wi' onset that the hypothesis calls strongest as a fragment.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: They will arrive on Friday unless the ferry is cancelled, so keep the gate unlocked until dark.
adversarial_test_results.detail: ' will' is the third named high-frequency w-function word: hypothesis predicts it stays under the active line in running English.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The manuscript is an unpublished novella by the Irish novelist Evelyn Vaughan, his only attempt at long fiction.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Near-miss of the Waugh example with the same author/novel frame and 'Evelyn' before the slot; the surname arrives as the single token ' Vaughan', so no token begins with w, and the only word fragments (' nov' | 'ella') are lowercase, outside rival 1's name-slot class.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The bill sits on the desk of Governor Tim Valdez, and it should be signed before the session ends.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Near-miss of the Walz example: identical bill-signing frame and ' Tim' before the slot, but the fragment is ' Val' | 'dez'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He then asked Ms. Cathy Milborn, the chief deputy, to certify the record and file it at once.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Near-miss of the Wilborn example: same 'Ms. Cathy X' clerk-list frame but the surname splits as ' Mil' | 'born' rather than ' Wil' | 'born'.

readings.explanation: The pole is a retrospective letter-w detector on the token it sits on: it fires when the measured token begins with w/W — short word-initial fragments and name pieces (' Wa', ' Wil', ' Wal', ' W', 'WH', 'wh', 'wi', the strongest of all), the written w of ordinary words ('whole', 'wolf', 'wing'; weaker but usually over the active line), and the w-letter of other scripts (kana 'ワーク'/'ワ'/'ヲ', which fires as strongly) — and the same response lands on the next token when a w ends a preceding word fragment ('ew'->'a' in Swahili, '-w'->'he' in 'two-wheeled'). It falls to the noise floor when the same slot carries the same word under any other initial letter ('Val' for 'Wal', 'golf' for 'wolf', 'short' for 'whole', 'groei' for 'werking' in Dutch), when the w sits inside the token ('answer', 'swim', 'between'), and it is weakest on the highest-frequency w-function words of running English ('was', 'with', 'will').

The pole detects any word-initial fragment token (a word-opening piece that must be continued) rather than the letter w specifically: it should fire nearly as strongly on non-w fragments in the same slot such as ' Val', ' Bal' or ' Zl' as on ' Wal' or ' Wil'.

The pole is a W-initial proper-name and acronym detector (Waugh, Walz, Wilborn, Wilhelmine, Wilken, the initial ' W.', FWHM, mathcal{W}), and the lowercase prose firings on ' whole' and ' whirled' are an unrelated offshoot: w-nouns in ordinary prose should stay below the active line.
